blocks.en: Planning Evangelistic Sermons – The Interview Method
blocks.es_reference: Planificación de Sermones Evangelísticos – El Método de la Entrevista
Idioma:
Vía:
Objetivo de Aprendizaje

blocks.en: After studying this unit you will be able to use the Interview Method taught in WiseSpeak to plan a complete evangelistic sermon.
blocks.es_reference: Después de estudiar esta unidad podrá usar el Método de la Entrevista enseñado en WiseSpeak para planificar un sermón evangelístico completo.
El Método de la Entrevista en WiseSpeak

blocks.en: WiseSpeak teaches that one of the most effective ways to plan an evangelistic sermon is the Interview Method. This method begins with real people and their stories. We imagine or recall an interview with someone who needs Christ. We listen to their questions, their struggles, and their needs. Then we let those real-life questions guide the sermon.
blocks.es_reference: WiseSpeak enseña que una de las formas más efectivas de planificar un sermón evangelístico es el Método de la Entrevista. Este método comienza con personas reales y sus historias. Imaginamos o recordamos una entrevista con alguien que necesita a Cristo. Escuchamos sus preguntas, sus luchas y sus necesidades. Luego dejamos que esas preguntas de la vida real guíen el sermón.
El Enfoque Inductivo

blocks.en: The Interview Method follows the inductive approach from the first seven units of WiseSpeak. We start with the specific facts in the text and work backward to discover the keyword and subject. The Interview Method makes the sermon personal and relevant. It forces the preacher to speak directly to the listener's actual situation. When combined with the keyword approach, the result is a clear, unified evangelistic message that feels like it was written for the person sitting in front of you.
blocks.es_reference: El Método de la Entrevista sigue el enfoque inductivo de las primeras siete unidades de WiseSpeak. Comenzamos con los hechos específicos del texto y trabajamos hacia atrás para descubrir la palabra clave y el tema. El Método de la Entrevista hace que el sermón sea personal y relevante. Obliga al predicador a hablar directamente a la situación real del oyente. Cuando se combina con el enfoque de la palabra clave, el resultado es un mensaje evangelístico claro y unificado que se siente como si estuviera escrito para la persona sentada frente a usted.
Cómo Funciona el Método de la Entrevista
Leer el texto elegido con cuidado.

blocks.en: Imagine interviewing an unsaved person who needs the truth in this passage. What question would they ask?
blocks.es_reference: Imaginar entrevistando a una persona no salva que necesita la verdad en este pasaje. ¿Qué pregunta haría?

blocks.en: Turn the main idea or answer into a plural noun keyword.
blocks.es_reference: Convertir la idea principal o la respuesta en una palabra clave (sustantivo plural).

blocks.en: Form the subject around the keyword.
blocks.es_reference: Formar el tema alrededor de la palabra clave.

blocks.en: List the specific answers or truths in the text. Turn each truth into a short point (five words or less) that is a singular of the keyword.
blocks.es_reference: Listar las respuestas o verdades específicas del texto. Convertir cada verdad en un punto corto (cinco palabras o menos) que sea un singular de la palabra clave.
Escribir un objetivo evangelístico de una sola oración.

blocks.en: Add a clear invitation at the end.
blocks.es_reference: Agregar una invitación clara al final.

blocks.en: The keyword is always a plural noun. Every point is a clean singular of that plural keyword. When a single verse does not contain every point needed, we add supporting texts from other passages while the keyword still holds the whole sermon together.
blocks.es_reference: La palabra clave es siempre un sustantivo plural. Cada punto es un singular limpio de esa palabra clave plural. Cuando un solo versículo no contiene cada punto necesario, agregamos textos de apoyo de otros pasajes mientras la palabra clave mantiene unido todo el sermón.

blocks.en: Example from John 4 — The Woman at the Well
blocks.es_reference: Ejemplo de Juan 4 — La Mujer en el Pozo

blocks.en: Suppose we are preaching from the story of the woman at the well in John 4. We imagine interviewing a person who feels empty and thirsty for something more. Their question might be, "How can I find real satisfaction in life?" The keyword is "sources" (a plural noun). The subject is "Three Sources of Real Satisfaction."
blocks.es_reference: Supongamos que estamos predicando de la historia de la mujer en el pozo en Juan 4. Imaginamos entrevistando a una persona que se siente vacía y sedienta de algo más. Su pregunta podría ser: "¿Cómo puedo encontrar verdadera satisfacción en la vida?" La palabra clave es "fuentes" (un sustantivo plural). El tema es "Tres Fuentes de Verdadera Satisfacción".

blocks.en: Question: How can I find real satisfaction in life? · Keyword: sources
blocks.es_reference: Pregunta: ¿Cómo puedo encontrar verdadera satisfacción en la vida? · Palabra clave: fuentes
Fuente Uno: Agua viva.
Fuente Dos: Verdadera adoración.
Fuente Tres: Testimonio personal.

blocks.en: Example from Luke 15 — The Prodigal Son
blocks.es_reference: Ejemplo de Lucas 15 — El Hijo Pródigo

blocks.en: Text: Luke 15:11–32 (the prodigal son). We imagine interviewing a person who has wandered far from God and feels ashamed. Their question might be, "Can God still accept me after what I have done?" The keyword is "reasons" (a plural noun). The subject is "Three Reasons God Welcomes You Home."
blocks.es_reference: Texto: Lucas 15:11–32 (el hijo pródigo). Imaginamos entrevistando a una persona que se ha alejado mucho de Dios y se siente avergonzada. Su pregunta podría ser: "¿Puede Dios todavía aceptarme después de lo que he hecho?" La palabra clave es "razones" (un sustantivo plural). El tema es "Tres Razones por las que Dios Te Recibe en Casa".

blocks.en: Question: Can God still accept me after what I have done? · Keyword: reasons
blocks.es_reference: Pregunta: ¿Puede Dios todavía aceptarme después de lo que he hecho? · Palabra clave: razones
Razón Uno: Amor del Padre.
Razón Dos: Brazos abiertos.
Razón Tres: Restauración completa.
Ejemplo de Romanos 5:8

blocks.en: We imagine interviewing a person who feels unworthy of God's love. Their question might be, "Why would God care about someone like me?" The keyword is "proofs" (a plural noun). The subject is "Three Proofs of God's Love."
blocks.es_reference: Imaginamos entrevistando a una persona que se siente indigna del amor de Dios. Su pregunta podría ser: "¿Por qué Dios se preocuparía por alguien como yo?" La palabra clave es "pruebas" (un sustantivo plural). El tema es "Tres Pruebas del Amor de Dios".

blocks.en: Question: Why would God care about someone like me? · Keyword: proofs
blocks.es_reference: Pregunta: ¿Por qué Dios se preocuparía por alguien como yo? · Palabra clave: pruebas
Prueba Uno: Cristo murió por nosotros.
Prueba Dos: Mientras éramos pecadores.
Prueba Tres: Dios demuestra amor.

blocks.en: Why the Interview Method Is Powerful for Evangelistic Preaching
blocks.es_reference: Por Qué el Método de la Entrevista Es Poderoso para la Predicación Evangelística

blocks.en: The Interview Method makes every sermon feel relevant. It answers the exact questions people are asking today. It keeps the message focused on one clear question and one clear answer. The one-sentence objective keeps the entire message aimed at conversion. This method works especially well when the text speaks to a universal human need.
blocks.es_reference: El Método de la Entrevista hace que cada sermón se sienta relevante. Responde exactamente a las preguntas que la gente se hace hoy. Mantiene el mensaje enfocado en una pregunta clara y una respuesta clara. El objetivo de una sola oración mantiene todo el mensaje apuntado a la conversión. Este método funciona especialmente bien cuando el texto habla de una necesidad humana universal.

blocks.en: Practical Steps to Use the Interview Method in Your Preaching
blocks.es_reference: Pasos Prácticos para Usar el Método de la Entrevista en Su Predicación

blocks.en: Choose a text that answers a real human struggle. Imagine interviewing an unsaved person who needs this truth, and write their question in one clear sentence. Then follow the seven steps above: form the subject by placing the keyword at the end, and prepare a clear invitation that calls for immediate response. This method, taught throughout WiseSpeak, turns the Bible into a personal conversation with the listener.
blocks.es_reference: Elija un texto que responda a una lucha humana real. Imagine que entrevista a una persona no salva que necesita esta verdad, y escriba su pregunta en una oración clara. Luego siga los siete pasos de arriba: forme el tema colocando la palabra clave al final, y prepare una invitación clara que llame a una respuesta inmediata. Este método, enseñado a lo largo de WiseSpeak, convierte la Biblia en una conversación personal con el oyente.

mc.stem: What sermon-planning method does this unit teach?
options: The Word Method
The Interview Method
The Question Method
The Textual Method

mc.stem: The Interview Method begins with:
options: A topic chosen apart from the text
A creed of the church
A famous quotation from a theologian
Real people and their stories

mc.stem: The Interview Method follows which approach?
options: Inductive — begin with the text's specific facts and work backward
Deductive — start with a topic and find proof-texts
Allegorical — find symbolic meaning behind the words
Anecdotal — start with a personal story about the preacher

mc.stem: What is the FIRST step in the Interview Method?
options: Form the subject around the keyword
Write the one-sentence evangelistic objective
Read the chosen text carefully
Add a clear invitation at the end

options: proofs

mc.stem: The keyword in the Interview Method must always be:
options: A verb in the imperative mood
A plural noun drawn from the text
A proper name from the passage
An adjective that describes God

mc.stem: The maximum length of each outline point is:
options: Twelve words
A full sentence of any length
Five words or less
Ten words or less

mc.stem: The Interview Method makes the sermon especially:
options: Personal and relevant — feels written for the person sitting in front of you
Academic and historical — heavy on cultural background
Theatrical and dramatic — performance-oriented in delivery
Cautious — avoids any direct call for decision

mc.stem: When a single verse does not contain every point, the Interview Method:
options: Reduces the sermon to a single point with no parallel structure
Adds supporting texts from other passages while the keyword still controls the outline
Switches to a deductive topical outline and drops the keyword
Abandons the keyword discipline entirely

mc.stem: What is the SECOND step in the Interview Method?
options: Add a clear invitation at the end
Form the subject around the keyword
Write the one-sentence evangelistic objective
Imagine interviewing an unsaved person who needs the truth in this passage

sa.prompt: Define the Interview Method in your own words.
sa.model: The Interview Method begins with real people and their stories: we imagine or recall an interview with someone who needs Christ, listen to their questions and needs, and let those real-life questions guide the sermon. We then choose a plural-noun keyword and build the points inductively.

sa.prompt: List the seven steps for using the Interview Method.
sa.model: The seven steps are: read the text, imagine the interview, draw out the person's question, select the plural-noun keyword, form the subject, build the short parallel points and objective, and close with the invitation.

sa.prompt: In the John 4 example, what is the imagined interviewee's question, what is the keyword, and what are the three points?
sa.model: In the John 4 example the interviewee's question is 'How can I find real satisfaction in life?' The keyword is 'sources,' and the three points are: living water, true worship, personal testimony.

sa.prompt: In the Luke 15 (prodigal son) example, what is the imagined interviewee's question, what is the keyword, and what are the three points?
sa.model: In the Luke 15 prodigal son example the question is 'Can God still accept me after what I have done?' The keyword is 'reasons,' and the three points are: the Father's love, His open arms, full restoration.

sa.prompt: In the Romans 5:8 example, what is the imagined interviewee's question, what is the keyword, and what are the three points?
sa.model: In the Romans 5:8 example the question is 'Why would God care about someone like me?' The keyword is 'proofs,' and the three points are: Christ died for us, while we were still sinners, God demonstrates His love.

sa.prompt: Why is the Interview Method described as inductive rather than deductive?
sa.model: The Interview Method is inductive because it begins with the specific facts of the text and the person's real question and works backward to the keyword and subject, letting the text speak rather than imposing an outside topic.

sa.prompt: Why is the Interview Method described as especially powerful for evangelistic preaching?
sa.model: The Interview Method is especially powerful for evangelism because it makes the sermon personal and relevant - speaking directly to the listener's actual situation and need, which makes the message memorable and aimed at conversion.

sa.prompt: How are the three outline points required to relate to the keyword?
sa.model: Each of the three points must be a short singular of the plural keyword, five words or less, and parallel in form - keeping the outline unified and memorable.

sa.prompt: How does the Interview Method handle the case when a single verse does not contain every point needed?
sa.model: When one verse does not contain every point, the Interview Method adds supporting texts, but the keyword still controls the outline so the added passages stay unified under one plural-noun keyword.

sa.prompt: According to this unit, what does the Interview Method turn the Bible into for the listener, and why does that matter for evangelism?
sa.model: The Interview Method turns the Bible into a personal conversation for the listener - the text answering his own real questions and needs. That matters for evangelism because it engages him directly and relevantly, moving him toward a personal decision rather than leaving truth abstract.
